questions: Are walkways usable in both directions simultaneously? That is, if there is a walkway from building (i,j) at floor X to building (i',j') at floor X, can it be traversed from (i',j') to (i,j) at floor X as well, assuming both buildings have at least X floors?

When moving via a walkway, does the action count as a stair usage? The prompt says the count of times using stairs is incremented each time he moves up or down one floor, but it does not explicitly state whether walkway moves count as zero stair uses.

Can Takahashi move multiple floors within a building using stairs in a single action, or must each floor transition be counted as one stair usage? The example given (1st to 6th floor counts as 5 uses) clarifies that each floor change is one use, but it's not explicit whether he can skip floors in one move.
Is it allowed to use a walkway to move to a building that has exactly X floors (i.e., the target floor is the top floor), or does 'at least X floors' include equality?

Can Takahashi stay on the same floor within a building without using stairs? For example, if he is on floor X and needs to move to an adjacent building also at floor X, does he need to use stairs to exit the building first?
Are there any constraints on the order of operations? For instance, must Takahashi alternate between stairs and walkways, or can he use multiple stair moves consecutively within the same building?

If Takahashi is on a floor X and wants to move to an adjacent building, but that building has fewer than X floors, can he use stairs to descend to a lower floor in his current building first, then use a walkway at that lower floor?

Is the goal to minimize only the number of stair usages, regardless of the number of walkway usages? Walkway usages are not counted in the cost, but could there be an implicit constraint like minimizing total moves or time?
